A CORRECTION, NOT A NEW ADJUDICATION. bmdb 1541 hostap batch 7 (src/pasn/pasn_responder.c .. src/tls/tlsv1_server_write.c). Same standard and method as batches 1-6 and 8 (see correction-api00c-644-hostap-b1-task1541), including ADR-0011's caller-check basis (aurora-lint bbf240e9): a function nothing outside the corpus can call, whose every call site provably tests the value for NULL, has a validated parameter. A dereference is not a test for that basis.

RESULT: 140 rows. 89 TP stand (reason restated to the TP basis; source unchanged) and 51 are corrected TP -> FP here, a flip rate of 36.4%. A fresh-context refuter reviewed all 61 proposed flips and upheld 51. It rejected the 10 RADIUS rows (radius.c:488/530/595/621/911/1566/1932/1953, radius_client.c:849/1943): the in-tree call sites all test msg or pass address-of values, but hostap ships src/radius as libradius.a for outside programs (radius_example/README: "used as a library in another program"; radius_example/Makefile links it), so under ADR-0011 their caller set is open, and those rows stay TP. The 23 tlsv1_client_*/tlsv1_server_* flips rest on tls_internal.c's dominating conn->client/conn->server tests; tlsv1_* is not declared in the public tls.h and is reached only through tls_internal.c.

Mechanics follow bmdb 1490/1531 and the 1541 pilot: in-place edits keep each key; task-644-full-reaudit takes a row_count decrement and a superseded_rows record.

Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision claim is made here.
